entries.subject: Size: JPL Small-Body Database diameter
entries.finding: 814 Tauris is drawn as a sphere at the 102.229 ± 2.138 km diameter the JPL Small-Body Database lists, with JPL's stated reference urn:nasa:pds:neowise_diameters_albedos::2.0[mainbelt] (http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJ...791..121M). DAMIT held no shape model for it on 2026-10-08, so the sphere is illustrative.

entries.subject: PDS SBN catalogue values that disagree with the factsheet or are not shown
entries.finding: Shown rotation "36.081 h" (jpl-small-body-database) differs from the LCDB V4.0 summary record 814 period 18.030 h (U 2, synodic); the shown value is kept.
entries.revisitWhen: A newer release of the named catalogue, or a review that replaces the shown value.

entries.subject: Tauris whole-disc color
entries.finding: Gaia Collaboration, Galluccio et al. (2023) published the mean of 5 Gaia epoch spectra of the unresolved disc: reflectance against the Sun in 16 bands from 374 to 1034 nm, 1 at 550 nm (0.962 at 462 nm, 1.006 at 638 nm). The sphere is painted in that one color (#424240 in sRGB) through the shared disc-integrated-color method, scaled to the 5.4% geometric albedo JPL lists (± 1.1%), from NEOWISE (Masiero et al. 2014, ApJ 791, 121; PDS bundle neowise_diameters_albedos 2.0). It is one mean, not a map. Tinaut-Ruano et al. (2023), A&A 669, L14, found Gaia DR3 reflectances slightly too red at wavelengths shorter than 550 nm; the bands are used as published, without that paper's correction.
